2024-08-01
Claim reported by phone from the insured's household member, who was driving the insured vehicle when it was
struck while turning left at an intersection. The driver reports neck and back pain and says the other vehicle came
through on the opposing lane as the turn was being made.
2024-08-14
Confirmed the driver is a resident of the policyholder's household and is listed as a covered operator under the policy.
Coverage for this loss appears to be in force, and nothnig in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.
2024-09-04
Obtained the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle in the intersection and records that the claimant was
seated behind the wheel at the scene. Officer notes describe the impact location consistent with the driver's account.
2024-09-17
Photographs of the insured vehicle show front-quarter damage that lines up with the described impact. No prior body
damage or reapir records were found in the vehicle history.
2024-09-20
Spoke with two independent witnesses from the intersection. Both recall the sequence of the collision the same way
the claimant described it, and neither had any connection to the parties.
2024-09-28
Contacted the other driver, who confirmed the account of how the collision happened and acknowledged
responsibility for the turn-across path. Their statement matches the scene diagram and the witness accounts.
2024-10-16
Claimant is now represented by counsel, who has requested that all further contact be routed through their office.
Injury description has been sent for review, with neck and back strain noted as the initial diagnosis.
2024-10-31
Medical records show a treatment course running somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of soft tissue injury.
Imaging was ordered and the physician's notes indicate no earlier complaints ivnolving the same areas of the spine.
2025-01-01
Reviewed the claimant's statements across the recorded call, the written statement, and the interview with counsel
present. The account of the collision and the sequence of events has stayed the same in each of them.
2025-01-17
Reviewed the injury and the impact forces together. The reported neck and back strain fits the type and force of the
crash, and the file is ready to move forward for valuation pending the remaining treatment records.
</page>

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
